discrepancy_explained: The divergence lived in src/resextract/dashboard/__main__.py (the file the card calls src/resextract/__main__.py; the top-level src/resextract/__main__.py did NOT exist). It computed allow_remote = args.allow_remote or (explicit_host and not is_loopback(host)) and then called the shared guard with allow_remote=True, so the guard's own logic was never a refusal for that path: it BOUND 0.0.0.0:8971 and 192.168.2.187:8972 with uvicorn's open read routes. The console script resolves to resextract.cli:main (pyproject [project.scripts]), and cli._resolve_serve calls check_bind_host(host, allow_remote) with only the user's flag, so `.venv/bin/resextract serve` and `python -m resextract.cli serve` refused with exit 2. Entry-point table (post-fix, --host 0.0.0.0, no --allow-remote): console exit 2 bound no | python -m resextract exit 2 bound no | python -m resextract.cli exit 2 bound no | python -m resextract.dashboard exit 2 bound no. exposure_recommendation: Honest exposure: with --allow-remote and a non-loopback bind the READ routes are reachable from the network — proven live: curl http://127.0.0.1:8974/ -> 200 AND curl http://192.168.2.187:8974/ -> 200 (the same response from the LAN), while only POST /api/control/* is token-gated. That is acceptable ONLY as a loud, explicit opt-in (the CLI prints 'WARNING binding non-loopback host ...; this exposes the dashboard'), but it is not 'safe': a token on the control routes does not protect the store, journals, dockets or graph. Recommendation: on a non-loopback bind, require the token on READ routes too (an auth dependency over the read handlers) or refuse to start without one. This is NOT a one-line change (read routes are ~12 handlers with no auth dependency), so it is left to the main session as a new unit; the closest one-line mitigation would be to require an explicitly supplied non-auto token whenever the bound host is non-loopback, which does not by itself gate reads.
